prologue.title: Prologue
prologue.body1: September 1926. You have just witnessed the resounding trial of Dr. Nadelmann, a person close to you, who was the rising star of the Department of Anthropology at Miskatonic University. Nadelmann is the only living member of the science expedition launched to explore a wild valley in northwestern Canada called North Hanninah. Sylvia Davidson, Norman Falkner and Bernard Epstein, the three newly graduated students who accompanied the anthropologist, have disappeared.
prologue.body2: The Arkham authorities were keen to ensure that justice was done, and Dr. Nadelmann was found guilty of involuntary homicide. However, everyone could see during the testimony that Nadelmann's physical and mental health were severely deteriorated. An ugly throat wound, still unhealed after weeks, prevented Nadelmann from speaking normally; when the words could be understood, they were implausible rants, full of man-eating monsters and local spirits that doomed the expedition. Standing in front of the court, many relatives of the missing students come to find you. They are desperate, and ask you to find the three students.
prologue.body3: Soon after, you follow the footsteps of the previous expedition, starting by train from Arkham to Central Canada. During the trip you read Dr. Nadelmann's expedition notebook. Several entries in, Nadelmann notes that the Sarcee guide of their expedition, Charlie Foxtail, abandoned the group after seeing the tracks of a being that Charlie called "The Wendigo". Then the writing becomes increasingly jerky, unreadable. Your destination is Fort McDonald, an outpost of the Mounted Police, which will give you access to the wild valley of North Hanninah. You have a short time before the arrival of winter.

setup.placeStartingLocations: Put the Fort McDonald, Jetty and Sarcee Territory locations into play. Each investigator begins play at the Jetty.
setup.placeNorthHanninah: Shuffle the 3 North Hanninah locations and put them into play, one directly to the north of the Jetty, one directly to the north of the first, and one directly to the north of the second.
setup.placeUncharted: Randomly take one of the Mountain Range cards and remove it from the game. Shuffle the remaining 6 locations and randomly put one into play directly to the east and one directly to the west of each North Hanninah location.
setup.studentsFateDeck: Take the story cards, story side up. For each pair of cards with the same name, remove one at random from the game. The 3 remaining cards named Sylvia's Fate, Norman's Fate and Bernard's Fate make up the Students' Fate deck. Set this deck aside.
setup.setAsideStories: Set the remaining story cards aside, out of play.
setup.setAsideAssets: Set Expedition Notebook, Sarcee Guide, Tomahawk, Ithaqua's Knowledge and all the Old Injury cards aside, out of play.
setup.tabletToken: If you don't have a {tablet} token in your chaos bag, add one for this game.

xp.glimpsedTheMythos: having glimpsed the Cthulhu Mythos in this remote, wild corner of the world

resolutions.noResolutionBody: The trip back to Fort McDonald is terribly trying. You do not have time to heal your wounds on the way, and must quickly leave this valley and its dangers. You finally manage to reach Fort McDonald, which you now perceive as a small island of human civilization in the midst of an ocean of wild darkness.
resolutions.resolution1Body: After a brutal fight, the Wendigo staggers back, and emits shrieks that no natural creature could produce. The more wounds it takes, the more its cries seem to come from a human in agony. You strike the final blow and see the terrible creature collapse. When you raise your head, the sight of your opponent leaves you astounded: it is the naked body of a man, lying close to you in a pool of blood, his claws and antlers gone, patches of fur and goat-like hoofs remaining. Somehow you make it back to Fort McDonald.
resolutions.resolution2Body: Officers listen to the story of your expedition with suspicion, then with amazement when they see the evidence you have collected. You return to Arkham without looking back, and share with the students' relatives the fate of their loved ones. Although they finally have the answers to their questions, some truths are too terrible to hear. Most end up thanking you for putting an end to this case.
resolutions.resolution3Body: Officers listen to your story, particularly attentive when you present them with material evidence of what happened. You return to Arkham exhausted, tormented by this experience, but alive. Although the students' families have some answers, the mysteries that remain will haunt them forever. The few truths unveiled will not be enough to remove the nightmares that have invaded your sleep.
resolutions.resolution4Body: Officers listen to the story of your expedition. You dare not tell them everything, lest they take you for a fool. You leave immediately, without looking back, and return to Arkham, prey to terrible nightmares. Having no answer to their questions, the students' relatives are plunged into torments that you understand too well.

epilogue.charlieBody: On the way back to Fort McDonald, Charlie confessed that he regrets abandoning Dr. Nadelmann and his students, and explains that ever since he left the party he was pursued by the monster that attacked him in the hut, which sensed his fear. He feels he did not deserve your kindness after what he did, and when you arrive back at Fort McDonald he bids you a fond farewell and offers you his weapon. "This weapon has been in my family for many generations. Your courage and wisdom far surpass my own; I know my ancestors would want you to have it. Go with honor, my friend."
epilogue.goldBody: After your return to Arkham you find a gold mining company and share your discovery. The men in charge are very interested, and offer to pay you a percentage of the profits from the Hanninah if you tell them where the seam is. As you sign your contract you remember the mad prospector, and what you had to do to be rid of him. You hope the future workers on the site will not suffer the same fate... or worse.
epilogue.ithaquaBody: When you deciphered all the inscriptions of the temple, Ithaqua found in you a vessel, a channel to our world. Now you are constantly beset with visions that come true, intuitions coming out of nowhere that turn out to be accurate. Your vision of the world has changed, and you have to struggle regularly to avoid falling into madness.
epilogue.normanAliveBody: Norman is alive and well, the only real survivor of the previous expedition. You managed to get him back to Fort McDonald, where he was taken care of by the Mounted Police doctor. He behaved strangely, and did not really answer the questions about what happened to him; obviously, he had lost his mind. He kept saying he had to announce an important piece of news to the whole world, but had to find the best way to do it. When you went home you tried to bring Norman with you, but he had already left the fort in the middle of the night. In a letter he left for you, he explains that he will return to Arkham — you can reassure his family about that — but that he has a lot to do before he can come home...
epilogue.normanDeadBody: When you found Norman there was something off about him, an inner force that could have led to your defeat. However, he was also the only surviving student you could have brought back alive. His death haunts you, but not as much as the tears of his relatives when you tell them that Norman succumbed on the return journey.
epilogue.nadelmann1Body: Shortly after your return to Arkham you ask to see Dr. Nadelmann, to tell the anthropologist that you managed to kill the Wendigo. When you arrive at the asylum you find that Nadelmann's injury has been healed for some time, and that the doctor's appetite and natural energy seem restored. Nadelmann listens distractedly to your story, seemingly busy with lunch. Some time later you learn that Dr. Nadelmann had to be locked in a separate cell, without further details. One morning the police come to ask you about the disappearance of Dr. Nadelmann. They explain that the psychiatrists found the cell empty: there were claw marks all over some ragged clothes, and the window had been brutally forced from the inside. You cannot give them a reasonable explanation, and they leave disappointed. Now you are tormented by the thought that it may not be possible to kill the Wendigo once and for all.
epilogue.nadelmann2Body: Dr. Nadelmann's appeal is held a few weeks after your return, and you present yourself with evidence to clear the anthropologist. You make a strong impression on your audience, and although there is unexplained evidence in this case, Dr. Nadelmann walks free from the hearing with full innocence established. Some time later you learn with satisfaction that Nadelmann will resume classes at the beginning of the next school year. The physical and mental after-effects still persist, though, with panic attacks every winter when the first snowflakes fall.
epilogue.nadelmann3Body: Shortly after your return to Arkham you visit Dr. Nadelmann to help prepare for the appeal. When you arrive at the asylum you find that the wound is still not healed, and the anthropologist is extremely thin now. Nadelmann asks you to tell the story of your expedition, and is very attentive to the details. Even though you had not planned to tell everything, you feel forced to confirm that the Wendigo is still in the valley. The news affects Nadelmann deeply, and when you leave you hope you have not undermined the anthropologist's morale too badly. A few days later you learn with great sadness that Dr. Nadelmann committed suicide in the asylum.
epilogue.nadelmann4Body: Dr. Nadelmann's appeal is held a few weeks after your return. You came hoping to exonerate the anthropologist. Unfortunately there is too much unexplained material in this case and the appeal is rejected. In addition, the mental state of the anthropologist is considered good enough after the few weeks spent in the asylum, so the police escort Nadelmann to Arkham prison to serve the sentence. Since then you often think back to Nadelmann, and feel a great pain knowing your friend is locked up for a long time, the anthropologist's life broken forever.
